title: Computational Foundations of Cognitive Neuroscience
institution: Draft textbook self-published at gershmanlab.com (the lecture slides give the author's affiliation as Harvard University)
description: Draft open textbook that 'provides an introduction to computational cognitive neuroscience' and 'attempts to unify many aspects of neural computation through the lens of decision theory'. Fifteen chapters, each a separate PDF: 1 Reverse engineering the brain; 2 Neural primitives of thought; 3 Principles of perceptual representation; 4 The Bayesian brain; 5 Approximate inference; 6 Attention; 7 Perceptual decisions; 8 Object categorization; 9 Plasticity as optimization; 10 Learning to predict; 11 Learning to act; 12 Predictive maps; 13 Simulation and planning with mental models; 14 Memory systems; 15 Generalization, geometry, and causality. The chapters opened end with study questions or references. Companion pages offer 15 lecture slide decks (PDF), 24 mini-project PDFs and five Python notebooks (for chapters 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9).
codeLicence: MIT License, 'Copyright (c) 2026 sjgershm' (github.com/sjgershm/CFCN: efficient_coding, costly_inference, neural_gibbs, attentional_cueing and backprop notebooks with requirements.txt; 13 commits)
rightsNotes: Textbook page: '© 2025 Samuel J. Gershman (CC-BY license)', the link pointing to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (read in the page HTML on 2026-10-31). The chapter PDFs print no licence of their own (chapter 1 checked).

The lectures, mini-projects and code pages carry no licence statement (their HTML was searched on 2026-10-31). Corniversity treats the lecture slides and mini-project PDFs as reference-only and imports only the textbook chapters (gershmanlab.com/textbook/chapterN.pdf).
CC BY 4.0 requires attribution: credit Samuel J. Gershman, link the licence and indicate changes.
The companion notebooks are MIT-licensed code (see codeLicence).

limitations: A draft 'subject to change': chapter files are replaced in place at the same URLs, so page locators can drift between updates. No publisher or print edition is named.
The date '10/05/2026' has no stated format; read in US order it is 5 October 2026.
Only chapters 1, 4 and 10 and lecture 1 were text-extracted; the other chapters are known by title only. The mini-project PDFs were not opened and the notebooks were not run.
Each chapter PDF is paginated from 1, with the running head 'chapter N <page>' from its second page; the first page of a chapter prints no page number.
The same pages are mirrored at gershmanlab.opalstacked.com; gershmanlab.com is the canonical host.
Import is limited to the textbook chapters: the lecture slides and mini-projects on the same host carry no licence statement.
